name: The spruce fringe
plain: Spruce grows dense right to the top of the granite, not as scattered cones: a dark edge just above the rock.

params.edge: dense to the rock's top edge

confidence: medium: curves from World's levels/downeast/coast_rules.json (21 Oct), checked against the Bar Harbor shore and cited above; Matt's field corrections still to come

sources.cite: Davis, R.B. (1966) Spruce-fir forests of the coast of Maine. Ecol. Monogr. 36: 79-94.
sources.note: red and white spruce with balsam fir to the edge of the rock on the outer coast
the rule's purpose, in his words

where_note: the fringe is the forest's edge on the rock, not the whole forest: from just above high water to ~14 m above it (derive.py's salt field reaches only a few metres inland, so height stands in for distance; the forest spawner and the canopy cover the rest)
